newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia's medical workers end six-week-long strike.
newsitem.headline: Serbia's medical workers end six-week-long strike.

text.p: Serbia's doctors and nurses ended a six week old strike after the government, fearing unrest by disgruntled patients ahead of crucial elections, promised to pay overdue wages.

"The trade union is satisfied with the agreement -- it fulfils all the demands over which the strike was started," Stevan Djordjevic, head of the health workers strike committee, told Reuters on Monday.
Doctors, nurses and other medical staff throughout Serbia have been on strike since May 12 over unpaid wages and what they say is general neglect of medical services.

"Thanks to a more regular and better inflow of funds into the republican social insurance fund and short-term government measures, we can guarantee that payment of wages to health workers will be in line with the signed agreement," Serbian Health Minister Leposava Milicevic was quoted by Belgrade media as saying.
Djordjevic said the strike had revealed numerous problems in hospitals and clinics, such as shortages of medicines, equipment and food for patients.
All health institutions were back at work on Monday, including the biggest outpatients' clinic of the Clinical Centre of Serbia, which closed its doors a week ago.
Pensioners also took to the streets for the first time earlier this month after the government, strapped for cash but committed to a tight fiscal policy, delayed pensions.

Independent trade unions and opposition parties have accused the government of dragging its feet on the strike to "buy time" ahead of crucial Serbian presidential and parliamentary elections by the end of the year.
